title: Fake Medicare Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare. They say your coverage will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may use scary language to pressure you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your coverage will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and bank information right now."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security or bank number
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups on Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus. It tells you to call a phone number for help. If you call, scammers ask for money or remote access to your computer.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft support now at 1-888-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up says you must call a number
Claims to be from Microsoft or Apple
Asks for payment or remote access
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number. If you’re worried, ask a trusted friend or family member for help.

title: Grandparent Scam: 'I'm in Trouble, Please Send Money!'
how_it_works: You get a call or text from someone pretending to be your grandchild. They say they’re in trouble and need money right away, often for bail or an emergency. They may beg you not to tell anyone.
example_message: "Grandma, it’s me! I’m in jail and need you to send $2,000 for bail. Please don’t tell mom and dad."
red_flags: Wants money sent by wire or gift card
Voice sounds off or caller is upset
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check if it’s real.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with a package delivery. The message has a link to click for more information. The link leads to a fake website that tries to steal your information.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to confirm your address: [fake link]"
what_to_do: Do not click the link. Delete the message.

title: Social Media Romance Scam
how_it_works: Someone you meet on Facebook or another site quickly declares love and asks for money. They often claim to be overseas or in the military. They make excuses why they can’t meet in person.
example_message: "I love you so much, but I need $500 to fix my car so I can come visit you."
red_flags: Asks for money or gift cards
Refuses to meet in person or video chat
what_to_do: Stop communicating and never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.
